title: Chapter 6961: Number One Immortal

Chapter 6961: Number One Immortal

Chapter 6961: Number One Immortal

“Hmm...” Tribulation Daoist had no idea where Li Qiye came from before glancing at the sky with a stern expression.

Li Qiye, on the other hand, focused on the statue.

“Are you interested in Mundane Immortal?” The daoist asked.

“Yes, it must be fate.” Li Qiye nodded.

“Do you know about her legends?” He asked.

“I do not.” Li Qiye shook his head.

“I have wine and stories. Are you interested in having a drink?” He knew Li Qiye was not a mortal.

“Can’t say no to that.” Li Qiye smiled.

“Good, let’s find a nice place then.” He laughed and led Li Qiye to a scenic area within the monastery.

One could observe the whole city while surrounded by verdant cliffs and lakes.

He prepared both wine and snacks. He poured a cup for Li Qiye and said: “I fermented this myself, give it a shot.”

“Not bad, not bad.” Li Qiye drank it in one gulp.

“Just not bad?” He became offended and slapped his gourd: “If my wine claims second place here, no other wine dares to claim first place.”

“Sure, in Survivor Realm.” Li Qiye smiled.

He turned red and smiled wryly: “I suppose I’m shallow for forgetting that there is always a high sky. I’ll punish myself with another cup, no, three.”

“Don’t have to be obvious, just drink.” Li Qiye pushed his empty cup over.

“Apologies for the delay, another three cups for punishment then.” He poured one cup for Li Qiye and gulped three down in a row.

“If this continues, you’ll finish the whole gourd by yourself.” Li Qiye shook his head.

“Haha, I’ll stop. Don’t worry though, my gourd contains a whole lake, we won’t run out.” He laughed.

Li Qiye chuckled and drank his wine.

“Young man, what was the finest wine you had drank?” He asked.

“Looks like you fancy drinking.” Li Qiye said.

“The truth is that I was a wine brewer in training before cultivating. By just smelling the wine, I know if it is going to be good or bad, that’s all I want to do in life, drink.” He said.

“I suppose that does add light to your life.” Li Qiye said.

“You still haven’t answered my question.” He reminded.

“Wine made from the primordial.” Li Qiye smiled.

“The primordial?” He blurted.

Li Qiye didn’t answer and spotted the statue from afar.

“Fine.” He smiled and said: “I did say I have wine and stories. Now it’s time for the stories, what are you interested in?”

“Start with Mundane Immortal then.” Li Qiye smiled.

“She came from outside, but I don’t know where exactly.” He stared at the statue as he spoke.

He paused for a moment, trying to read Li Qiye’s reaction. Alas, the guy was sipping his wine nonchalantly.

“She became the savior of our world and its people.” He sighed.

“Not Myriad Tribulations Sect?” Li Qiye asked.

“Of course, our progenitor, Myriad Tribulations Immortal, was another savior.” He smiled wryly.

Li Qiye stared at him in silence.

“Rumor has it that certain events happened unexpectedly, it’s all vague.” He smiled wryly.

“We have time and wine.” Li Qiye said.

He poured another full cup and spoke: “The only thing that was left after the war was Heaven Pit. Since our world is nearby, it barely survived. Some lives persevered.”

“It must have been difficult.” Li Qiye said.

“So they said. The world wasn’t as calm as it is now. Lightning and flame descended randomly and destroyed villages. Everyone lived in fear, always in a state of alert...” He continued: “Fortunately, a youth appeared with a body capable of enduring and accepting the tribulations. He cultivated and became an immortal.”

He seemed proud while speaking of his progenitor.

“Myriad Tribulations Immortal.” Li Qiye said.

“Yes, he then absorbed the remaining tribulations in our world, allowing the sky to shine again.” He said.

“Impressive, capable of absorbing tribulations in this whole realm.” Li Qiye nodded.

“That’s not all he did, he used his immortal power to build this world again. It is due to his effort that we can live in peace.” He said.

“Yes, using the word, savior, is appropriate here.” Li Qiye said: “Ordinary immortals couldn’t have done this.”

“The progenitor was the first immortal and the strongest.” He said.

“First, sure. Strongest, not necessarily.” Li Qiye smiled.

“If he leaves this world, he’ll still be one of the top immortals.” He had confidence in his progenitor.

Li Qiye didn’t respond.
